title: Learning tricky words by shape and story
examples: How do I learn tricky words?
Why can I not sound out said?

explain.say: Some words do not play fair. Look at said on the board. Sound it out and you might say sayd. But we say it to rhyme with red. So we learn it a different way.

explain.say: Look at the middle part glowing: a and i. In most words, they make the sound in rain. But in said, they sneak off and make the sound in egg. That is the tricky bit. Can you point to it?

explain.say: Now the shape trick. Draw a box around said with your finger. Trace each letter and say its name: s, a, i, d. Your eyes are taking a photo of the shape. Snap!

explain.say: Now the story trick. Make a silly sentence from the letters: Sally Ate Ice-cream Daily. The first letters spell said! Silly stories stick in your memory. Can you say it with me?

faq.a: A tricky word has a part that does not follow the usual sound rules. Said, was, the and you are tricky words.

faq.q: How do I learn a tricky word?
faq.a: Find the tricky part, trace the shape of the word, and make up a silly story from its letters. Then read it lots of times.
asks: How do I remember tricky words?

faq.q: What is the tricky part of said?
faq.a: The a and the i. They usually make the sound in rain, but in said they make the sound in egg.
It is a silly sentence where each word starts with a letter of the tricky word. Sally Ate Ice-cream Daily spells said.

faq.q: How often should I practise tricky words?
faq.a: A little every day is best. Practise a few tricky words at a time on cards. A teacher or grown-up can play a matching game with you.
asks: How many tricky words should I learn?

facts: Said, was, the and you are all among the hundred most common words in English.
In the word said, the letters ai make the same sound as the e in egg.

quiz.say: Which part of said is the tricky part?
quiz.why: The a and i make the sound in egg, not the sound in rain.

wrong.0: The s makes its usual sound, like in sun.
wrong.2: The d makes its usual sound, like in dog.
